author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Fall color in New Hampshire’s White Mountains may arrive later than usual but last longer, according to regional foliage forecasters interviewed by the Conway Daily Sun.

Forecasters pointed to healthy, full canopies and improved moisture after earlier drought conditions as reasons for optimism. They expect color to progress by elevation from late September into the middle of October rather than peak everywhere at once.

The outlook remains weather-dependent. Warm sunny days followed by crisp nights can help leaves produce vivid reds and oranges, while a hurricane, severe storm or strong wind event could remove leaves before peak color. Daylight loss, temperature and moisture all influence the timing.

For visitors and tourism businesses, a longer progression can spread travel across several weekends. Routes through the Kancamagus Scenic Highway, Pinkham Notch, Franconia and Kinsman Notch are among the areas expected to draw foliage traffic. The forecast is not a guarantee; travelers should check current foliage maps and local conditions before choosing a destination.
dek: Healthy canopies and improved moisture conditions could support bright color from late September into mid-October, depending on elevation and weather.
headline: White Mountains forecasters expect later, longer foliage season
